text: Mental and emotional health
is just as important as heart health.
Heart failure can come as a big shock
and be difficult to come to terms with.
Start by talking with your healthcare team
about how you're feeling.
You may feel stressed, angry, anxious, or teary,
and not be sure why.
Keep up any hobbies and spend time with loved ones.
Be sure to talk to someone if you're feeling down.
If you are feeling sad or miserable
for many days in a two week period,
it is vital to go and see your doctor.
You may be experiencing depression,
which is common and manageable with help.
You might be concerned about returning to work,
financial pressures, and keeping medical appointments.
Don't be afraid to ask your healthcare team
for information on what social, financial,
and medicine support might be available to you.
Heart rehabilitation or exercise programs
can help build your confidence in being more active
and learn more about looking after your heart.
You may also meet other people living with heart failure
and share ideas about getting on with your life.
Speak with your healthcare team about a referral,
and to learn more about managing heart failure,
watch the other videos in this series.
